title: Exact pooled count-time and terminal-number quotient through a CIR-Poisson kernel
statement: For m bosonic modes with constant isotropic bath b=kappa nu/theta, d=b+kappa, a well-defined [H_t,K]=0, supplied thermal total-number law, and pooled aggregate monitored-loss instrument J_t(rho)=theta c_t sum_j a_j rho a_j^dagger with known predictable 0<=c_t<=c_max and theta c_t<=d, the Poisson kernel K|S=s~Poisson(s/theta) intertwines the no-count and detected-count instruments with the CIR signal. Thus the full aggregate count-time record and terminal physical total photon number K have exactly the CIR-Cox record plus terminal Poisson(S_T/theta) law.

requires: All monitored output ports are pooled and all aggregate count times are exposed; no port label is supplied.
Constant isotropic thermal bath rates b=kappa nu/theta and d=b+kappa.
Initial K distribution equals that of the supplied product thermal state; the simplest stated initialization is the product thermal state with nu/theta photons per mode.
Hamiltonian is well defined, number-preserving, and remains so under the shared record-dependent control.
provides: Exact branchwise generator/count-map intertwining, including no-count backaction and actual removal of the detected photon.
Exact joint law of full pooled aggregate count record and terminal K as a CIR Cox record and conditional terminal Poisson draw.
A proved joint TV bound epsilon for (record,S_T) transfers unchanged to (record,K); the root filter supplies such a bound under its own separate assumptions.
assumptions: m is a positive integer mode count; theta,kappa,nu>0; c_t predictable from the observed aggregate record and shared independent randomness; theta c_t<=d.
Number-preserving interactions, including hopping and cross-Kerr terms, may be strong but cannot change total K.
The conservative nonexplosive evolution and adequate operator domains are supplied; no domain theorem for arbitrary unbounded Hamiltonians is asserted.
costs: The exact quotient itself has no additional quartic bridge error. Finite-bit root solving, Poisson sampling, arithmetic, and detector/bath calibration are supplied or separately charged; this is not a learned physical interface.
contract.units: Photon number K is dimensionless; S is in scaled intensity units; theta is the scaling in K|S~Poisson(S/theta).
contract.obstruction: Does not predict full conditional quantum state, port/interference labels, individual-mode number under general hopping, or the unobserved K path. Does not permit replacing a coarse latch-bin observation by unobserved fine count times. H_t cannot steer K, so this is not general nonlinear quantum control.

body: The Hamiltonian contribution vanishes in the quotient because [H_t,K]=0; this explains why strong number-preserving interactions cannot steer K. The Poisson kernel intertwines the detected-count map as well as the generator, so the result is an instrument identity rather than a moment match. The gamma-root posterior can be projected to K by composing its PGF with w(z)=beta theta/(beta theta+1-z). The U986 dependency applies only when consuming its compressed-root error/memory guarantee; the instrument identity itself does not require pruning.

review.scope: Exact conservative quantum number-instrument/Poisson intertwining under supplied thermal total-number distribution, constant isotropic bath, complete pooled monitored losses, shared known predictable efficiency and [H_t,K]=0. Only aggregate count times and terminal K are represented. Number-preserving H cannot steer K; this is not general nonlinear control.
